subject: Commit ladder & uplift negotiation — MAP milestones and close timeline
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Romero <jessica.romero@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Commit ladder & uplift negotiation — MAP milestones and close timeline

Hi Jessica and team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great discussion on where Redwood can help reduce inference cost and stabilize latency for your clinician-facing workflows. Per our conversation, attached is an updated Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a draft SOW that tie evaluation milestones to commercial triggers so we can align ramp and pricing. High-level summary: 

- Evaluation window: 6 weeks (pilot start target: 11/16) with two technical gates (integration + throughput).
- Pilot pricing: 50% off hosted API rate for capped pilot tokens (up to 1.2M tokens).
- Commit ladder (volume+timing triggers):
  * Stage 1: 100k/month commit (month 1-3) — base rate A
  * Stage 2: 250k/month commit (month 4-6) — 12% discount vs base
  * Stage 3: 500k/month commit (month 7-12) — 22% discount vs base
- Renewal / uplift mechanics: baseline renewal assumes committed band remains; if sustained usage exceeds committed band by >20% for two consecutive months, we propose a true-up at then-current rates capped to +10% uplift relative to the committed unit price (i.e., a bounded uplift).

Attachments: Vantage_MAP_v3.pdf, SOW-Vantage-Draft.docx, Pricing-worksheet-VH.xlsx.

Ask: Can you review the MAP and confirm the pilot start window (week of 11/16) and whether the proposed uplift cap is acceptable to procurement? If helpful we can run a short call with procurement and your security team next week to review the data retention and audit log controls in the private deployment option.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment(s): Vantage_MAP_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB), SOW-Vantage-Draft.docx (DOCX, 48KB), Pricing-worksheet-VH.xlsx (XLSX, 22KB)
From: Jessica Romero <jessica.romero@vantagehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@vantagehealth.com>, VantageHealth Procurement <procurement@vantagehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commit ladder & uplift negotiation — MAP milestones and close timeline

Thanks Mina — appreciate the clear MAP. A few notes from our side after an internal review: 

1) Procurement is asking for a deeper initial discount if we commit to a 12-month ramped commit (they cited budget constraints). Specifically they want either 20% off Stage 2 pricing or a guaranteed credit if we hit Stage 3 earlier.
2) Our security and compliance team asked for clarity on data retention windows and audit log export for the pilot (we have to confirm SOC2 artifacts).
3) On the uplift cap: procurement is wary of any automatic true-up that could increase cost at renewal beyond a nominal band. They asked whether Redwood can set an absolute cap on renewal uplift (e.g., not exceed +5% year-over-year) or provide a multi-year price hold tied to a minimum aggregated commit.

Would you be open to a short call with procurement + security next Thursday? Also, Carlos will upload procurement redlines to the SOW and share them in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Jessica Romero
Director, Product Ops
Vantage Health
jessica.romero@vantagehealth.com

On Sun, Nov 1, 2026 at 9:12 AM Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [original message and attachments]
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Commit ladder & uplift negotiation — internal counter proposal

Team — quick internal take to prepare for procurement call. My suggested commercial position to present: 

1) Preserve pilot economics (50% off capped tokens) to remove initial friction. Pilot is promotional customer acquisition.
2) Move to a time-bound ladder discount (as Mina proposed) but make Stage 2 guarantee contingent on 6 months of observed usage. Offer a one-time accelerator credit if they hit Stage 3 in month 6 (e.g., $25k credit applied to month 7 invoice).
3) Uplift at renewal: offer a bounded true-up but shift from % uplift to a blended absolute per-unit cap — e.g., max $0.0025 per token increase on renewal vs committed unit price, which in practice keeps YOY increases under ~8% for their expected volume profile. This satisfies procurement sensitivity and preserves Redwood's ability to price for growth.
4) Include a true-up/true-down mechanism in the SOW with an audit window (30 days after quarter end) to reconcile over/under usage.

Operational asks: confirm whether Dedicated capacity is a requirement for the pilot or whether we can run an initial pilot in our hosted environment with an NDA + SOC2 artifacts. If they require private deployment from day one that will push timelines/cost.

I'll draft a redline to the SOW and a short slide summarizing the commit ladder + uplift cap for the call. Mina — can you propose 2 slots for a procurement/security sync?

— Priyom
VP Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Nov 3, 2026 at 11:40 AM Jessica Romero <jessica.romero@vantagehealth.com> wrote:
> [Vantage feedback pasted]
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Romero <jessica.romero@vantagehealth.com>, Carlos Vega <c.vega@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commit ladder & uplift negotiation — MAP milestones and close timeline

Jessica / Carlos — thanks for the quick review. Attached is a revised MAP and an updated SOW that incorporate our counter-proposals: 

- Pilot: unchanged (50% off, 1.2M token cap).
- Commit ladder update: if Vantage commits to a 12-month ramp target (aggregate 3-6-12 month bands documented in SOW) Redwood will:
  * Increase Stage 2 discount to 15% (from 12%) if the aggregate 3-month trailing usage meets the Stage 2 band within the first 6 months.
  * Provide a $25k accelerator credit if Stage 3 is achieved by month 6.
- Renewal uplift: Redwood will commit to a bounded uplift mechanism capped to the lesser of (a) +10% of committed unit price OR (b) an absolute per-unit increase of $0.0025. That cap applies to the first renewal after the initial 12-month term.
- True-up: quarterly reconciliation with a 30-day audit window; credits issued within next invoice cycle.

We believe this is a fair middle ground: it gives Vantage visibility and protection on renewal movement while preserving upside if Vantage materially scales. If procurement still needs a strict +5% lock, we can explore a minimum aggregated commit guarantee in exchange for a deeper multi-year price hold — happy to sketch the trade-off live.

Proposed next steps:
- Procurement/security sync (30–45 min) — propose Thu 11/12 10:00 AM PT or Fri 11/13 9:00 AM PT.
- If procurement agrees, sign SOW and target pilot start 11/16.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

From: VantageHealth Procurement <procurement@vantagehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Jessica Romero <jessica.romero@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@vantagehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commit ladder & uplift negotiation — MAP milestones and close timeline

Mina — thanks for the revised MAP and for walking us through the approach. Procurement has reviewed the SOW and attached redlines (Vantage_Procurement_Redlines.pdf). Key asks from procurement/legal: 

1) Reduce maximum renewal uplift to +5% for the first renewal OR accept a 24-month price guarantee in exchange for a stronger discount on Stage 2.
2) Add explicit data retention limits for pilot logs and require a monthly export capability for audit in the SOW.
3) Clarify termination for convenience terms and add a 30-day wind-down obligation for any Dedicated deployment to preserve access to cached models and KV state.
4) Procurement requests an initial EDI for invoices and a standard 60-day net payment term (they will consider 45 days if accelerator credits are applied early).

We are generally aligned on the MAP milestones but procurement needs the uplift exposure limited or offset via a longer-term guaranteed price. Can Redwood produce a short modeling table showing the three options (A: +5% renewal cap, B: +10% cap with minimum 12-month aggregate commit, C: 24-month price hold with 18% Stage 2 discount) so our CFO can sign off? Also we expect to run the pilot in Hosted first; Dedicated would be considered after the pilot if performance warrants.

Please let us know when you can send the three-option modeling table and we will route the SOW to legal for final redlines. Looking forward to the procurement/security sync later this week.

Regards,
VantageHealth Procurement
procurement@vantagehealth.com
